claim: AWS DataSync is an online data movement service that simplifies and accelerates data migrations to AWS and helps you move data quickly and securely between on-premises storage, edge locations, other cloud providers and AWS storage.
question: What is AWS DataSync?

values.display: online data movement service
between on-premises storage, edge locations, other cloud providers

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync is an online data movement service that simplifies and accelerates data migrations to AWS and helps you move data quickly and securely between on-premises storage, edge locations, other cloud providers, and AWS Storage.

claim: AWS DataSync is a secure, reliable, high-speed file transfer service that helps you transfer file or object data to, from and between AWS storage services.
question: How does the DataSync user guide define the service?

values.display: secure, reliable, high‐speed file transfer service
to, from, and between AWS storage services

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync is a secure, reliable, high‐speed file transfer service that helps you quickly and easily transfer your file or object data to, from, and between AWS storage services.

claim: DataSync uses an AWS-designed transfer protocol, decoupled from the storage protocol, to accelerate data movement; its network optimizations include incremental transfers, in-line compression, sparse file detection, and in-line data validation and encryption.
question: Which network optimizations does DataSync perform?

values.display: incremental transfers, in-line compression, and sparse file detection
AWS-designed transfer protocol

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync employs an AWS-designed transfer protocol—decoupled from the storage protocol—to accelerate data movement. The protocol performs optimizations on how, when, and what data is sent over the network. Network optimizations performed by DataSync include incremental transfers, in-line compression, and sparse file detection, as well as in-line data validation and encryption.

claim: The DataSync agent connects to existing storage using NFS and SMB, to a Hadoop cluster as an HDFS client, to self-managed object storage or Google Cloud Storage using the Amazon S3 API, and to Azure Blob Storage using the Blob API, and writes into an S3 bucket, EFS file system or FSx file system.
question: How does a DataSync agent connect to source storage systems?

values.display: industry-standard NFS and SMB protocols
to your Hadoop cluster as an HDFS client

evidence.quote: The DataSync agent connects to your existing storage systems using the industry-standard NFS and SMB protocols, to your Hadoop cluster as an HDFS client, to your self-managed object storage or Google Cloud Storage using the Amazon S3 application programming interface (API), or to Azure Blob Storage using the Blob API. The agent transfers data rapidly and writes it into your designated Amazon S3 bucket, Amazon EFS file system, or Amazon FSx file system.

claim: When copying data to Amazon S3, DataSync converts each file to a single S3 object in a 1:1 relationship and preserves POSIX metadata from NFS shares or HDFS as S3 object metadata; when you copy such objects back to file formats the original file metadata is restored.
question: How does DataSync map files to S3 objects and keep metadata?

values.display: single S3 object in a 1:1 relationship
preserves POSIX metadata

evidence.quote: When copying data to Amazon S3, DataSync automatically converts each file to a single S3 object in a 1:1 relationship, and preserves POSIX metadata from NFS shares or HDFS as Amazon S3 object metadata. When you copy objects containing file system metadata back to file formats, the original file metadata (that DataSync copied to S3) is restored.

claim: All data is encrypted in transit between the DataSync agent and the DataSync service using TLS, and DataSync supports default at-rest encryption for Amazon S3 buckets and encryption of data at rest and in transit for Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx.
question: How does DataSync encrypt data?

values.display: encrypted in transit between the DataSync agent and
default at-rest encryption for Amazon S3 buckets

evidence.quote: All your data is encrypted in transit between the DataSync agent and the DataSync service using Transport Layer Security (TLS). DataSync supports using default at-rest encryption for Amazon S3 buckets. DataSync also supports encryption of data at rest and in transit for Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx.

claim: For each transfer DataSync performs integrity checks both in transit and at rest, to ensure that the data written to the destination matches the data read from the source.
question: What integrity checks does DataSync perform for each transfer?

values.display: integrity checks both in transit and at rest
matches the data read from your source

evidence.quote: DataSync ensures that your data arrives intact. For each transfer, the service performs integrity checks both in transit and at rest. These checks ensure that the data written to your destination matches the data read from your source, validating consistency.

claim: A DataSync agent is a virtual machine (VM) appliance that DataSync uses to read from and write to storage during a transfer.
question: What is a DataSync agent?

values.display: virtual machine (VM) appliance
read from and write to storage

evidence.quote: An *agent* is a virtual machine (VM) appliance that DataSync uses to read from and write to storage during a transfer.

claim: DataSync provides two types of agents, one that handles Basic mode tasks and another that handles Enhanced mode tasks.
question: How many types of DataSync agent exist?

values.display: two types of agents
Basic mode tasks and another handling Enhanced mode

evidence.quote: DataSync provides two types of agents, with one handling Basic mode tasks and another handling Enhanced mode tasks.

claim: You can deploy a DataSync agent in your storage environment on VMware ESXi, Linux KVM, Nutanix AHV (using the KVM agent image) or Microsoft Hyper-V, and for storage in a VPC in AWS you can deploy the agent as an Amazon EC2 instance.
question: Where can a DataSync agent run?

values.display: VMware ESXi, Linux Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM)
deploy an agent as an Amazon EC2 instance

evidence.quote: You can deploy an agent in your storage environment on VMware ESXi, Linux Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM), Nutanix AHV (using the KVM agent image), or Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisors. For storage in a virtual private cloud (VPC) in AWS, you can deploy an agent as an Amazon EC2 instance.

claim: A DataSync task describes a transfer: it identifies a source and a destination location along with details about how to copy data between them. A task execution is an individual run of a task.
question: What are a DataSync location, task and task execution?

values.display: identifies a source and destination location
an individual run of a DataSync transfer task

evidence.quote: A *task* describes a DataSync transfer. It identifies a source and destination location along with details about how to copy data between those locations.
A *task execution* is an individual run of a DataSync transfer task.

claim: During a task execution DataSync prepares, transfers and verifies your data.
question: What happens in a DataSync task execution?

values.display: prepares, transfers, and verifies your data
During a task execution

evidence.quote: During a task execution, DataSync prepares, transfers, and verifies your data.

claim: Basic mode tasks prepare, transfer and verify your data sequentially, while Enhanced mode tasks do these in parallel.
question: How do Basic and Enhanced mode differ in running the prepare, transfer and verify phases?

values.display: prepare, transfer, and verify your data sequentially
Enhanced mode tasks do these in parallel

evidence.quote: Basic mode tasks prepare, transfer, and verify your data sequentially, while Enhanced mode tasks do these in parallel.

claim: By default DataSync prepares a transfer by scanning the contents and metadata of both the source and destination locations to identify differences between them.
question: How does DataSync decide what to transfer on a repeated run?

values.display: examining your source and destination locations
identify differences between the two

evidence.quote: DataSync by default prepares your transfer by examining your source and destination locations to determine what to transfer. This is done by scanning the contents and metadata of both locations to identify differences between the two.

claim: If you configure a task to transfer all data, DataSync does not compare the source and destination locations; the execution still has a PREPARING status while DataSync scans the source.
question: What does DataSync do in the prepare phase when the task transfers all data?

values.display: doesn't compare your source and destination locations
PREPARING status

qualifiers.condition: the task is configured to transfer all data

evidence.quote: If you configure your task to transfer all data, DataSync doesn't compare your source and destination locations. Your task execution still has a `PREPARING` status, though.

claim: When you only transfer data that has changed, DataSync does not transfer a file that exists in both locations and has not been modified in the source since the previous task execution.
question: Does a later DataSync run copy unchanged files again?

values.display: hasn't been modified since the previous task execution
only transferring data that has changed

qualifiers.condition: the task transfers only data that has changed

evidence.quote: There's a file that exists in your source and destination locations. The file in the source hasn't been modified since the previous task execution. Since you're only transferring data that has changed, DataSync doesn't transfer that file next time you run your task.

claim: If an object exists in both locations and changes in the source, DataSync skips it in the destination when the task is not configured to overwrite data in the destination.
question: Does DataSync overwrite a changed destination object by default?

values.display: your task doesn't overwrite data in the destination
DataSync skips this object in your destination

qualifiers.condition: the task is not set to overwrite data in the destination

evidence.quote: An object that exists in both of your locations changes in your source. When you run your task, DataSync skips this object in your destination because your task doesn't overwrite data in the destination.

claim: DataSync skips an object in the source that uses an archival storage class and has not been restored; you must restore an archived object for DataSync to read it.
question: Can DataSync read an archived S3 source object that was not restored?

values.display: You must restore an archived object for DataSync
archival storage class and isn't restored

qualifiers.scope: DataSync source objects in archival storage classes

evidence.quote: DataSync skips an object in your source location that's using an archival storage class and isn't restored. You must restore an archived object for DataSync to read it.

claim: DataSync always performs integrity checks on your data during a transfer, and at the end of a transfer it can also check just the transferred data or the entire dataset in both locations.
question: Does DataSync always verify data during a transfer?

values.display: always performs integrity checks on your data during
just the transferred data or the entire dataset

evidence.quote: DataSync always performs integrity checks on your data during a transfer. At the end of a transfer, DataSync can also perform additional checks on just the transferred data or the entire dataset in both locations.

claim: When checking data integrity DataSync calculates and compares the checksum and metadata of the files, objects or directories in the locations, and verification fails with an error if it finds differences.
question: What does DataSync compare when it verifies data?

values.display: calculates and compares the checksum and metadata
verification fails with an error

evidence.quote: When checking data integrity, DataSync calculates and compares the checksum and metadata of the files, objects, or directories in your locations. If DataSync notices differences between locations, verification fails with an error.

claim: When transferring between AWS storage services in the same account, in the same Region or across Regions in the same partition, no agent is required, and the data stays in the AWS network without crossing the public internet.
question: Is a DataSync agent needed to copy between AWS storage services in one account?

values.display: no agent is required
doesn't traverse the public internet

qualifiers.scope: DataSync between AWS storage services in the same account

evidence.quote: When transferring between AWS storage services in the same account (whether in the same AWS Region or across AWS Regions in the same partition), no agent is required. Your data remains in the AWS network and doesn't traverse the public internet.

claim: You pay for data transferred between AWS Regions with DataSync; it is billed as data transfer out from the source Region to the destination Region.

values.display: data transfer OUT from your source Region
You pay for data transferred between AWS Regions

evidence.quote: You pay for data transferred between AWS Regions. This is billed as data transfer OUT from your source Region to your destination Region.
